wording: Discussing a new idea with someone often helps me understand my own thinking more clearly.
After spending a long time interacting with others, I prefer a period with fewer conversations or activities.
I prefer having some activity around me while I work on a routine task.
When an activity is already under way, I usually wait for an opening before joining.
In shared settings, I tend to divide my attention among several people.
I prefer to form my thoughts before expressing them on a complex topic.
After a long quiet period, becoming active again usually helps restore my energy.
Before deciding what I think, I prefer time to consider the information on my own.
When several conversations are available, I prefer moving between them.
I prefer a low-activity setting when I need to think something through.
At the start of a shared task, I tend to ask others for their first thoughts.
Between demanding activities, I usually restore my energy by spending some quiet time.
I often share an idea while I am still working out its details.
I prefer giving sustained attention to one or two conversations at a time.
I often enjoy settings where several things are happening at once.
When I am still forming an answer, I prefer to wait briefly before expressing it.
When a task is unclear, I usually make sense of it by talking through possible approaches with someone.
In a new shared task, I prefer some context before asking others for input.
